title: Fixed ei ole with singular owners
summary: Use fixed ei ole with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä when possession is denied.
objectives: Use fixed ei ole with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä when possession is denied.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Use fixed ei ole with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä when possession is denied.
Minulla ei ole palloa means “I do not have a ball”. The owner phrase does not require en ole: possession keeps ei ole.
keyPoints: Use fixed ei ole with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä when possession is denied.

examples.english: I do not have a ball.
steps: For possession, ei supplies “not” and ole is the form of olla after it. Keep ei ole together; minulla does not require en ole.
The complete noun form palloa (“a ball”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with singular owners” lesson.

examples.english: You do not have a book.
steps: sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Use sinulla ei ole, not sinulla et ole. The owner phrase does not conjugate the negative verb.
The complete noun form kirjaa (“a book”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with singular owners” lesson.

examples.english: She does not have a dog.
steps: hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Hänellä ei ole can mean “she does not have” or “he does not have”. Both use the same negative frame.
The complete noun form koiraa (“a dog”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with singular owners” lesson.

examples.english: I do not have a cat.
steps: Changing the thing leaves the fixed ei ole frame unchanged.
The complete noun form kissaa (“a cat”) is shown here; its formation is taught in the “Regular negative noun forms with singular owners” lesson.

examples.english: He or she does not have a car.
steps: hänellä identifies the singular owner in this fixed ei ole with singular owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
autoa (“a car”) is the complete regular singular partitive: auto + -a.

examples.english: I do not have a pillow.
steps: minulla identifies the singular owner in this fixed ei ole with singular owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
tyynyä (“a pillow”) is the complete regular singular partitive: tyyny + -ä.

commonMistakes: Keep both words ei ole: ei alone leaves the negative possession pattern incomplete.
Use the complete noun form shown in these verb questions; the partitive lesson teaches how to form it.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with minulla, sinulla and hänellä; do not change it to en or et.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
kynä + -ä = kynää. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed ei ole in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “You do not have a game.” Address one person. Use sinulla (“you as the owner”) and peliä (“a game”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Sinulla does not change the fixed possession pattern ei ole. Peliä is the supplied negative noun.
